messages:
Maya: Heads up — hit a weird backlog in us-west-2. Small inference jobs are sitting in queue for 7+ minutes while one large model export occupies a handful of GPUs. Dashboard shows node-level GPU util: most nodes ~5%, one pool pegged at ~98%. https://dash.redwood.example/hosts/abc
Henry: any recent scheduler changes?
Maya: not that I know of. CI shows a deploy 2am that touched admission heuristics but commit looked minor. ops-bot: Alert: queue_length(us-west-2, inference) > 500 for 00:12:34.
Sriram: Can you paste the scheduler decision log for an affected job? want to see placement/affinity.
Maya: pasted below (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-18T10:47:01Z] job=job-8343 req_gpus=1 pref_pool=gpu-pool-a policy=FIFO
[2026-03-18T10:47:01Z] admitted_job=job-12999 req_gpus=8 gid=export-2026 high_priority=false
[2026-03-18T10:47:02Z] queue_position(job-8343)=432
[2026-03-18T10:47:02Z] decision=defer reason=capacity_hol_lock
```
Maya: Looks like a long-running multi-gpu job grabbed the front of the FIFO and the admission logic won't backfill because of gang_affinity checks.
Tina: That matches a regression I worried about — we tightened gang-affinity checks last week to prevent noisy colocations. Side effect: no backfill permitted when first job requests >1 gpus and preemption disabled.
Henry: ah. So head-of-queue big job blocks all single-gpu short jobs even if nodes with free GPUs are available -> uneven util. We saw similar pattern but thought it was admission starvation.
Sriram: Repro idea: submit 1 long 8-GPU job with policy FIFO, then flood 100 single-GPU quick jobs; measure admit rate. I can run on staging.
Maya: repro script (staging):
```bash
# submit big job
submit_job --gpus 8 --duration 3600 --pool gpu-pool-a --policy fifo
# flood small jobs
for i in $(seq 1 200); do submit_job --gpus 1 --duration 30 --pool gpu-pool-a --policy fifo & done
```
Tina: temporary mitigation: enable backfill_override or allow partial-gang scheduling so small jobs can backfill free slots. But watch correctness for affinity-sensitive workloads.
Henry: Can we flip backfill_override in us-west-2 for a short window? Risk: might violate some placement guarantees for exports but reduces SLA violations for 99p latency.
Lorena: I'm +1 for targeted flip if we monitor. Add a safety guard: auto-revert in 10m and evict if export jobs missing GPUs.
Kyle: I'll push a canary via infra-toggle:
```json
{"region":"us-west-2","feature":"backfill_override","value":true,"ttl":600}
```
ops-bot: Change queued: backfill_override=true for us-west-2 by Kyle. Will auto-revert in 600s.
Henry: running load repro now against canary. posting metrics in ~5m.
Sriram: also opening a small bug PR to relax the gang-affinity short-circuit: add an allowance for partial backfill when queued job size > X and idle_slots >= Y.
Tina: please include unit test for affinity fallback. PR link?
Sriram: https://git.redwood/repo/scheduler/pull/4321 (draft)
Maya: good progress, thanks. After canary we saw admit rate for small jobs jump from ~2/min to ~45/min and percentile tail dropped. Will keep monitoring.
Lorena: can someone add a follow-up to eng-oncall to evaluate long-term fix vs feature flag?
Henry: tagging @eng-oncall. also we should schedule a postmortem if this escalates.
Maya: closing loop for now — will update if the auto-revert causes regressions. :thumbsup:
